title: Teams and Roles
html:
Goal: before the flywheel starts, settle who uses which account and on which console. The server checks separation of duties by username on every sign-off in the flywheel, so this step decides whether the next six phases are really done by different people.

Prerequisites

  • Environment Setup and Console Tour is done: at least one member can sign in to the team's console V3 as admin.
  • Roles and Separation of Duties is done: you have checked that workspace default has release mode gated.

1. Confirm your team's host console (5 minutes)

4–5 people per team. The organiser deployed one environment per team, so your team's host console is the ConsoleUrl the organiser gave your team: every member opens its ConsoleUrl/v3 and works in console V3. The whole team works on that console, so signing, admitting and releasing are really done by different people. Pick one member as the host (no debate needed, use a simple rule: the member with the lowest seat number in the team), who signs in as admin (approves registrations, grants permissions, reads spend and decision history).

Working alone is fine too: as in the Roles chapter, sign in to the five accounts in five different browser profiles (or private windows) and play each role in turn. The server still checks separation of duties by username, so every sign-off has to be done in the window of the matching account.

2. Roles and accounts (10 minutes)

Separation of duties is enforced by the server by username: whoever writes the criteria cannot sign them, an annotator cannot decide the calibration, and whoever asks for a release cannot sign it. Every role must therefore be held by a different person on their own account; sharing an account switches separation of duties off.

Role Account Stages and actions Permissions needed
Developer developer Builds and deploys the agent, drafts and publishes criteria, runs evaluations and regression replays, configures the drift watch, generates recommendations and fixes criteria.manage, agents.deploy, eval.run (member defaults)
Business owner biz-owner Signs criteria, curates and seals the golden set, admits candidates, decides judge calibration criteria.sign, golden.admit, judge.calibrate
Release ops release-ops Signs (or blocks) the release, approves waivers, rolls back if needed release.sign, waiver.approve
Domain expert sme Second annotator for calibration; writes correct answers on a reviewer link none extra
Facilitator / administrator (the team lead can double up) admin Adds accounts or approves registrations, grants permissions, checks and adjusts the release policy, creates calibration annotation tasks and issues annotation links, writes Cedar policies on the Gateway, reads spend and decision history, keeps time administrator

3. Hand out the accounts (10 minutes)

Three ways to hand out accounts — pick one:

Option A: the seeded accounts. The host gives the passwords of the four accounts developer, biz-owner, release-ops and sme from the organiser to the matching members; each person uses only their own. Fastest, and identical to the earlier chapters.

Option B: admin adds the accounts. The host signs in as admin, opens Modules → Configuration → User Management (/v3/users) and, for each member, clicks Add user in the page header: Username in the "team-role" format of section 4.1 of Roles and Separation of Duties (for team 3: t3-bizowner, t3-developer, t3-releaseops, t3-sme), Email an address such as t3-bizowner@example.com, Role Operator for release ops and Member for the others, the rest left at the defaults, then Create account. Click Copy on the one-time password that appears and hand it to that member privately. The account is active at once, with no approval; the full steps, screenshots and measured results are in section 6.3 of the Organizer deployment guide. Then click the permission chips for the business owner and the domain expert as in step 3 of Option C below; release ops created as Operator already holds release.sign and waiver.approve and not agents.deploy by default (DEFAULT_BY_ROLE in backend/app/services/users.py), so it needs no chips.

Option C: self-registration plus admin approval. Closer to a real team's request flow:

  1. Members open the host ConsoleUrl, click REGISTER on the sign-in page, and fill it in using the format from section 4.1 of Roles and Separation of Duties: username as "team-role", for example team 3's business owner enters t3-bizowner and company email t3-bizowner@example.com (the other roles likewise: t3-developer, t3-releaseops, t3-sme), plus a password of at least 8 characters that they write down. Click Create account. Expected result: the card title changes to Waiting for approval with Status Pending approval (measured with t3-bizowner).

  2. The host signs in as admin and opens Modules → Configuration → User Management (/v3/users) in the left navigation; the top of the page says "1 account is waiting for approval." (or "N accounts are waiting for approval.") and the Awaiting approval tile shows the count. Click Approve on the applicant's row (or open the account and click Approve in its header); in the Approve account dialog, workspace default under Workspaces is already selected, keep it, and click Approve. Expected result: a toast "t3-bizowner was approved." and Valid until reads 6 day(s) left · <approval date plus 7 days>.

  3. Grant the sign-off permissions. In the User Management list click the member's row to open the account, and click chips in the Agent permissions card: one click grants (the chip gets a tick and lights up), another click revokes. Every click shows "Permissions updated for <username>."; the monospace text to the right of each chip label is the permission key. Click these chips per role:

    Member Click on (grant) Click off (revoke)
    Business owner t3-bizowner Sign criteria criteria.sign, Admit to golden set golden.admit, Decide calibration judge.calibrate Manage criteria criteria.manage, Deploy agents.deploy
    Release ops t3-releaseops Sign releases release.sign, Approve waivers waiver.approve Deploy agents.deploy
    Domain expert t3-sme — Manage criteria criteria.manage, Deploy agents.deploy
    Developer t3-developer — —

    Expected result: for t3-bizowner (measured), after these 5 clicks Sign criteria, Admit to golden set and Decide calibration carry a tick, Manage criteria and Deploy do not, and every other chip keeps its default (Approve promotion, Approve waivers and Sign releases without a tick, all the rest with one).

    In the image: 1 Sign criteria; 2 Admit to golden set; 3 Decide calibration (granted); 4 Manage criteria; 5 Deploy (revoked).

  4. The seeded release-ops has the operator role; for a member account the Role card of V3 User Management offers only Make administrator, so a registered member account cannot be turned into an operator. To have release ops as an operator, create the account with Option B and pick Operator under Role. A self-registered member account also works: with Sign releases and Approve waivers from the previous step it can sign the release gate and approve waivers; the previous step also switched off its agents.deploy, otherwise that person could change the prompt and release it themselves, which is exactly what the operator role prevents.

If several teams share one console, prefix every resource with the team number, e.g. team 3: agent t3-hotel-concierge, knowledge base t3-hotel-policies, criteria t3-hotel-criteria, golden set t3-hotel-golden.

4. How to use this table in the flywheel

The steps in the next six phases read like "biz-owner signs" or "release-ops signs the release". In a team that means the member who holds that account: they do their step in their own browser, and everyone else refreshes their own window to see the result. The table on The Agent-DLC Flywheel landing page lists the main accounts of each phase; check it before a chapter to see who needs to be at the keyboard.

Checklist

  • The whole team can open the same host console at ConsoleUrl/v3
  • Every role is held by a different member on their own account; no shared accounts
  • The business owner holds criteria.sign, golden.admit, judge.calibrate; release ops holds release.sign, waiver.approve
  • If several teams share one console, the team prefix is agreed

Troubleshooting

Symptom Cause Fix
A member cannot sign in after registering: "This account is waiting for administrator approval." Registration requires approval admin clicks Approve in User Management
The account is approved but signs in to a No workspace granted page default was deselected at approval Grant default under Workspace access in the account detail
The business owner sees no Sign / Admit button Sign criteria criteria.sign / Admit to golden set golden.admit not granted Click those chips on in Agent permissions, section 3 step 3
